body:
- Compounding the firm's own figures, FY19 and FY20 together give about -66.9%, against about -12.7% for the Nifty 50 TRI. An FY18-end investor was at about 0.83x after FY21 and about 1.03x after FY22, so roughly four years with no gain. The Nifty 50 TRI went to about 1.81x over the same four years. A long-run 22% vs 18% CAGR edge therefore hides a period that would have broken most retail holders. Redemptions near the bottom also mean the dollar-weighted (investor) return is likely far below the time-weighted figure.
- Volatility is extreme in both directions: +152% in FY21 after -51% in FY20. That fits a concentrated (10–12 stock) micro/small-cap book with a high beta to small-cap liquidity cycles, plus stock-specific governance risk (LEEL).
- His edge seems to be early discovery of neglected small caps and turnarounds, plus a public following that adds price impact. That following is also a hazard for retail copycats: they buy after the bulk-deal disclosure and the move, often at worse prices, and they lack his information and exit timing.
- His business model is a fee-earning PMS/AIF (2% plus 10% over a 10% hurdle) built on a celebrity reputation, alongside proprietary investing. His media profile is a marketing asset for the PMS.

`theme:sector-auto-components` · confidence: single-source · tickers: MOTHERSON, BOSCHLTD, SONACOMS, BHARATFORG, UNOMINDA, ENDURANCE, SUNDRMFAST, BALKRISIND

**How it makes money:** Content-per-vehicle x OEM volume; aftermarket replacement; exports to global OEMs/Tier-1s.

**Metrics that matter:**
- Revenue growth vs OEM production (outperformance)
- Order wins (lifetime revenue) & conversion
- EBITDA margin & RoCE
- Export share & US/EU mix
- EV/powertrain-agnostic % of revenue
- Top-customer concentration
- Working-capital days

**Value chain and where margins sit:** Raw materials -> Tier-2/3 -> Tier-1 (system integrators) -> OEM; plus aftermarket distribution. Margins are best in proprietary systems, aftermarket and replacement tyres/batteries, and worst in build-to-print castings.

**Cycle drivers:** OEM production cycles (domestic + global), commodity prices, FX, US/EU tariffs, EV transition, China+1.

**Lead indicators (public India data):**
- SIAM/Vahan
- ACMA half-yearly industry data
- US Class 8 truck orders (ACT/FTR)
- EU ACEA registrations
- S&P Global light-vehicle production outlook

**What separated winners from losers:** Winners: rising content-per-vehicle, customer and geography diversification, powertrain-agnostic or EV products, disciplined M&A. Losers: single-OEM dependence, ICE-only parts, debt-heavy acquisitions, low-RoCE capex.

**Valuation ranges and peaks/troughs:** P/E 12–20x (cyclical forgings/castings), 25–50x (EV, electronics, aftermarket franchises). Peaks: 2017–18, 2021, 2024. Troughs: FY20 (BS-VI + slowdown), Mar 2020.

**Current state (Nov 2026):** Sona Comstar Q2 FY27 PAT ₹223 cr (+29%), revenue +35%, EV >50% of sales. Sundram Fasteners Q2 FY27 PAT ~₹160–173 cr (+13–14%; sources differ). Indian auto-part exports to the US have faced a 25% tariff since 2025, and ACMA said new US supply contracts were in limbo.

**Classic traps:**
- Lifetime order-win figures with unclear conversion
- Exporters' FX gains read as operating improvement
- EV-supplier valuations ahead of volumes
- Tariff-driven pre-buying

`case_study:dixon-technologies-2019-2025` · tickers: DIXON · confidence: verified

IPO Sep 2017 at ₹1,766 (≈₹353 after the 2021 5:1 split; first weekly close ₹532). From the Aug 2019 low ₹393 → ATH ₹18,398 (Jan 2025) ≈47x; P/E 39.5 → 197 (5x) × implied EPS ~9.4x. ₹13,054 on 19 Nov 2026 (−29%; low ₹9,920 Apr 2026, −46%). Drawdowns: −54% (2017–19), −52% (Nov 2021–Feb 2023). Early signal: Oct 2020 the subsidiary was approved under the mobile-phone PLI scheme, when phones were only ~12% of revenue; Dec 2020 a Motorola manufacturing agreement, then Nokia, later Samsung/Xiaomi/Vivo work. Revenue ₹4,400 cr (FY21) → ₹38,860 cr (FY25) → ₹48,873 cr (FY26); OPM stayed only 3–5%, but ROCE was 25–40% because the business is asset-light. A policy announcement plus named customer contracts were public months before the numbers. Stalled: mobile PLI ended Mar 2026; more than 80% of the business is now mobile; P/E reached ~190 at the peak and is ~51 now; follow-on 'PLI 2.0' was still being designed in Aug 2026. Lesson: policy-created volume is real EPS, but thin-margin contract manufacturing at 150–200x assumes the subsidy-era growth never ends. Watch the scheme's sunset date.

Key data: **start_year**: 2019; **end_year**: 2025; **start_price**: 393; **end_price**: 18398; **price_nov2026**: 13054; **multiple**: ~47x (≈52x from adjusted IPO price); **pe_start**: 39.5; **pe_end**: 197.1; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~9.4x; **max_drawdown**: -52% (2021-23); **early_signals**: PLI approval Oct 2020; Motorola deal Dec 2020; **ended**: PLI sunset Mar 2026, P/E 197→51; **lesson**: track scheme sunset; thin-margin EMS ≠ 150x
